blockers.title: Zero AC anchor references across 20 new/modified test files
blockers.problem: All 20 new/modified test files in this commit range contain ZERO AC-FRXXXX-YY or AC-NFRXXXX-YY anchor references in test function docstrings. This violates test-plan §1.4.1 (each test function must carry a spec-qualified AC anchor), acceptance AC-FR1601-02 (each test function must map to at least one valid AC with spec-id), and NFR-1101 AC-2 (static/diff review must not find import-only or untraceable tests). Approximately 1013 test functions across these files have no bidirectional AC traceability.
blockers.fix: Add AC-FRXXXX-YY or AC-NFRXXXX-YY annotations to the first line of each test function's docstring. Map each test to the specific acceptance criteria it exercises. For example, admin_routes tests should reference AC-FR1501-04 (AD-01), forms tests should reference AC-FR1501-05 (AD-02), repository tests should reference AC-FR1501-06 (AD-03), etc. For helper/formatting tests, map to NFR-1101 AC-1 (normal path + failure/boundary path coverage).

blockers.title: Duplicate test function: test_resolve_lightning_price_unknown_ref defined twice
blockers.problem: The function `test_resolve_lightning_price_unknown_ref` is defined at both line 226 and line 302 with identical implementations. The second definition silently shadows the first. pytest will only collect and run the second definition. This is a DRY violation and dead code. The first definition's coverage is never exercised.
blockers.fix: Remove the duplicate definition at either line 226 or line 302. Keep only one instance.

blockers.title: Brittle __get__ descriptor protocol binding for private method testing
blockers.problem: Tests use `InitWizardService._compose_gateway_url.__get__(svc)` and `StrategyRuntimeManager._extract_symbols.__get__(mgr)` to bind private methods to stub instances. This pattern: (a) depends on CPython descriptor protocol internals, (b) tests private methods directly rather than through public API, (c) will silently break if the class hierarchy changes, and (d) the `_StubSvc` class (line 10-11 of init_wizard_helpers) is empty but receives bound methods that rely on `self` attributes that don't exist on the stub. While the tests may pass because the methods don't use `self` attributes, this is fragile and could mask real bugs.
blockers.fix: For pure functions that don't use `self`, test them as module-level functions or via `@staticmethod`/`@classmethod` decorators. For methods that need `self`, either use the real class with proper init mocks, or refactor the production code to make these helpers testable via public API.

issues.title: Extensive use of assert out is not None without behavioral verification
issues.problem: Many tests (especially for UI component renderers and route handlers) use `assert out is not None` as their sole assertion. While this is partially acceptable for FastHTML component renderers that return complex HTML trees, it provides zero behavioral verification beyond 'didn't crash'. NFR-1101 AC-1 requires at least one normal path and one failure/boundary path with assertions on output, state, persistence, exception, or boundary calls. For renderer-only functions, consider asserting specific HTML content, CSS classes, or structural properties.
examples: test_v0204_b08_admin_routes.py:24 `assert out is not None` assertions out of ~40 test functions
test_v0204_b08_forms.py:15+ `assert out is not None` assertions out of ~20 test functions
test_v0204_b08_routes.py:30+ `assert out is not None` assertions out of ~50 test functions
test_v0204_b08_home_1.py: Multiple `assert out is not None` assertions for OverviewCards, AssetSummary, PositionInfo, OrderTable, PositionTable renderers
issues.fix: For renderer functions, add assertions on rendered HTML content: check for specific CSS classes, data attributes, or text content that the spec requires. For route handlers with redirects, assert on specific redirect locations and error/success query parameters. For empty/null input cases, `assert out is not None` is acceptable as a minimum sanity check but should be paired with at least one content assertion.

issues.title: pass placeholder tests that register coverage without exercising behavior
issues.problem: Several tests contain only `pass` as their body. These tests register as 'passing' and contribute to coverage numbers but exercise zero production code. NFR-1101 AC-2 explicitly prohibits empty pass tests, import-only tests, and self-fulfilling expected values. These tests inflate the test count and coverage metrics without actually validating anything.
instances: test_v0204_b08_live_1.py:131-132 test_live_position_info_with_positions (pass; comment 'Skipped: requires real Position-like objects')
test_v0204_b08_live_1.py:153-154 test_live_trade_panel_no_args (pass; comment 'Skipped: TradePanel requires portfolio_id')
test_v0204_b08_routes.py:702 test_admin_users_list_with_message_inserts_alert (pass; comment 'Skip — admin routes are inline')
issues.fix: Either: (a) implement the actual test with proper mocks/fixtures, (b) use `pytest.skip('reason')` with a GitHub issue link (per anti-pattern #2), or (c) remove the test if the code path is genuinely untestable in unit tests and document why in the test plan.

issues.title: No-assertion exercise-only tests
issues.problem: `test_run_daily_bars_sync_success` (line 65) has comment 'No assertion; just exercise the path.' `test_run_daily_snapshot` (line 110) and `test_run_market_snapshot` (line 114) call the function but make zero assertions. These tests exercise code paths for coverage but never verify the outcome. If the function silently returns without doing anything, the test still passes. This is a coverage-only test that violates NFR-1101 AC-1.
issues.fix: Add assertions that verify the expected side effects: check that the mocked db.store.update was called, that _save_job_history was called with correct arguments, or that the function completed without raising. For the snapshot tests, verify that the expected snapshot methods were invoked.

issues.title: Implicit db fixture dependency without local conftest.py
issues.problem: Both files use a `db` fixture parameter that is not defined in a local `conftest.py` under `tests/unit/quantide/web/pages/system/`. The `db` fixture is defined in `tests/unit/quantide/web/auth/test_v0204_b08_repository.py` (line 13) as a local fixture, not a conftest. The `web/conftest.py` has `init_app_state_for_web_tests` (autouse) but no `db` fixture. The datasource tests reference `db` as a fixture parameter but the fixture may be resolved from a shared conftest higher in the tree. If this works, it's by accident — the fixture source should be explicit.
issues.fix: Either add a `db` fixture to `tests/unit/quantide/web/conftest.py` for the web subtree, or add a `conftest.py` under `tests/unit/quantide/web/pages/system/` with the `db` fixture.

issues.title: test_v0204_b08_strategy_helpers.py: _pl_strat.DataFrame() returns empty DataFrame — tests assert row count only
issues.problem: `test_build_strategy_rows_empty`, `test_build_strategy_rows_with_class_no_portfolios`, and `test_build_strategy_rows_class_no_doc` use `_pl_strat.DataFrame()` (empty DataFrame) with `mock_db.get_portfolios_by_strategy = MagicMock(return_value=mock_df)`. The tests assert `len(rows) == 1` which only checks that a strategy with no portfolios still renders a row. The coverage comes from the empty DataFrame path, not the data-rich path. The `test_build_strategy_rows_portfolios_no_height` test (line 1410) uses `mock_df = MagicMock(spec=['is_empty'])` with `mock_df.is_empty = MagicMock(return_value=True)` — this is testing against a mock of polars DataFrame API, not the real DataFrame behavior.
issues.fix: Use real polars DataFrames with actual data for the data-rich paths, and verify specific cell content (strategy name, description text, portfolio count) rather than just row count.
